'''Lars Hesselholt''' (born September 25, 1966) is a [[Danes|Danish]] mathematician who works as a professor of mathematics at [[Nagoya University]] in [[Japan]], as well as holding a temporary position as Niels Bohr Professor at the [[University of Copenhagen]].<ref name="cv">[http://www.math.ku.dk/~larsh/cv/cv.pdf Curriculum vitae], retrieved 2015-02-18.</ref><ref name="bohr">[http://www.math.ku.dk/english/about/news/hesselholt/ Hesselholt receives Niels Bohr professorship], Univ. of Copenhagen, Dept. of Mathematical Sciences, July 12, 2012, retrieved 2015-02-18.</ref> His research interests include [[Homotopy|homotopy theory]],<ref name="acad"/> [[algebraic K-theory]],<ref name="acad"/> and arithmetic algebraic geometry.<ref name="bohr"/>

Hesselholt was born in [[Vejrumbro]], a village in the [[Viborg Municipality]] of Denmark.<ref name="cv"/> He studied at [[Aarhus University]], earning a bachelor's degree in 1988, a master's degree in 1992, and a Ph.D. in 1994;<ref name="cv"/> his dissertation, supervised by [[Ib Madsen]], concerned [[K-theory]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=43964}}</ref> After postdoctoral studies at the [[Mittag-Leffler Institute]], he joined the faculty of the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1994 as a [[C.L.E. Moore instructor]], and stayed at MIT as an assistant and then associate professor, before moving to Nagoya in 2008.<ref name="cv"/> Hesselholt's wife is Japanese, and when he joined the Nagoya faculty he became the first westerner with a full professorship in mathematics in Japan.<ref name="bohr"/>{{citation needed|date=April 2025}} He is the managing editor of the ''Nagoya Mathematical Journal''.<ref>[http://projecteuclid.org/editors/euclid.nmj Editorial board], ''Nagoya Mathematical Journal'', Project Euclid, retrieved 2015-02-18.</ref>

Hesselholt became a [[Sloan Fellowship|Sloan fellow]] in 1998,<ref>[http://www.sloan.org/sloan-research-fellowships/past-fellows/ Past fellows] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161106043224/http://www.sloan.org/sloan-research-fellowships/past-fellows/ |date=2016-11-06 }}, Sloan Foundation, retrieved 2015-02-19.</ref> and was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 2002.<ref>{{citation
 | last = Hesselholt | first = Lars
 | contribution = Algebraic $K$-theory and trace invariants
 | mr = 1957052
 | pages = 415–425
 | publisher = Higher Ed. Press | location = Beijing
 | title = Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, Vol. II (Beijing, 2002)
 | year = 2002}}.</ref> In 2012, he became one of the inaugural fellows of the [[American Mathematical Society]],<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2015-02-18.</ref> and a foreign member of the [[Royal Danish Academy of Sciences and Letters]].<ref name="acad">[http://www.royalacademy.dk/da/Members/356 Member profile] {{Webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20150219060939/http://www.royalacademy.dk/da/Members/356 |date=2015-02-19 }}, Royal Danish Academy of Sciences, retrieved 2015-02-18.</ref><ref>[https://www.math.nagoya-u.ac.jp/en/research/prize.html Recent prize recipients], Univ. of Nagoya, Graduate School of Mathematics, retrieved 2015-02-18.</ref>
